newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo's Agrobanka converts short term farm loans.
newsitem.headline: Yugo's Agrobanka converts short term farm loans.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Agrobanka bank will convert 72.45 million dinars ($12.09 million) worth of short-term loans to primary agricultural producers into long-term loans for constant working capital, news agency Tanjug said on Tuesday.

The credits will be extended for a three-year period for both crop and livestock production with a six-month grace period calculated from June 30 to December 31. The first three-month annuity matures on March 31, 1998.
Livestock production credits could be extended to five years. The bank will make a decision about this by January 1998.
The monthly interest rate equals the National Bank of Yugoslavia discount rate of 2.5 percent increased by 30 percent of the discount rate value.
Agrobanka will decide about the conversion of the short term into long term credits separately for each client by determining the level of their due liabilities on June 30.
It will take into account their financial capability to repay the reprogrammed debt.
